rows.text: Kenrith is a toolbox, not a reason to spend every turn reanimating the same creature. Establish mana and an independent draw source, then choose between interaction, counters, theft, token pressure, and recovery. The black ability is a fallback when a useful creature dies; the deck does not need a stocked graveyard to operate.

guide.title: Choose the job before spending the mana

rows.name: Kenrith, the Returned King
rows.text: the red ability gives ALL creatures haste and trample, including opponents' creatures. Green places a counter on any target creature; white gives any target player five life; blue draws a card for any target player. Black returns a creature under its OWNER'S control, so it does not steal an opponent's creature from a graveyard.

You do not need all five colors to cast Kenrith: his mana cost is four generic and one white, and he is a white permanent. Develop green for ramp, blue for draw and counters, and white for Kenrith and protection; find black and red when their specific tools are needed. Do not count Kenrith's five-color identity as five colors for a mana creature.

rows.name: Training Grounds + Biomancer's Familiar
rows.text: reduce the generic costs of creature abilities. One two-mana reducer makes Kenrith's green ability cost G, lifegain cost W, draw cost 1U, and reanimation cost 2B. With both, draw reaches U and reanimation reaches B. Colored mana requirements remain.

rows.name: Agatha of the Vile Cauldron
rows.text: growing her with Kenrith or Bill increases the discount on your creature abilities. She can also pump other creatures and grant haste and trample when Kenrith is unavailable. Her discount does not help noncreature permanents.

rows.name: Zirda, the Dawnwaker
rows.text: a normal card in the deck, not the companion. Discounts nonmana activated abilities across card types: Profane Procession, Shorikai, Clues, and creature abilities. Costs cannot fall below one mana. Creature-only reducers do not discount artifacts or enchantments unless they are also creatures on the battlefield.

rows.name: Seedborn Muse
rows.text: refreshes lands, mana creatures, and other permanents during every opponent's untap step. Reserve mana for interaction first, then spend leftovers before the next untap. Muse creates repeated opportunities, not infinite mana and not permission to ignore timing restrictions.

rows.name: Wilderness Reclamation
rows.text: untaps your lands during your end step after a productive main phase. Float mana before the trigger resolves if you want to combine it with mana from the newly untapped lands in the same end step. It does not untap your mana creatures or Shorikai.

guide.title: Build mana that also supports the rest of the deck

rows.name: Birds of Paradise + Delighted Halfling
rows.text: early acceleration fixes Kenrith and your engines. Halfling's colored mana is limited to legendary spells and cannot pay Kenrith's activated abilities; its colorless mode can pay generic activation costs.

rows.name: Bloom Tender + Faeburrow Elder
rows.text: count the actual colors of your permanents. Kenrith contributes white, Agatha contributes red and green, and Familiar contributes green and blue. Neither mana creature automatically produces five colors just because your commander has a five-color identity.

rows.name: Incubation Druid + Kenrith, the Returned King
rows.text: give Druid one counter with Kenrith instead of paying its five-mana adapt cost. It then taps for three mana of a single type one of your lands could produce. Kenrith can grant it haste, but the counter activation and haste still need mana before it starts producing.

rows.name: Bristly Bill, Spine Sower + Incubation Druid
rows.text: a landfall counter activates Druid's three-mana mode without Kenrith. Fetchlands provide two separate landfall events, letting the second counter go onto Bill, Agatha, or another relevant creature.

rows.name: Kinnan, Bonder Prodigy
rows.text: adds one extra mana whenever you tap a nonland permanent for mana. Druid's three becomes four, Sol Ring's two becomes three, and Waterskin can produce two each turn it untaps. Kinnan does not add one per mana already produced and does not double lands or Smothering Tithe's token creation.

rows.name: Bender's Waterskin
rows.text: refreshes itself on each opponent's untap step even without Muse, providing colored mana for interaction or discounted abilities. Muse and Waterskin do not produce two separate usable untaps during the same untap step.

rows.name: Nature's Lore + Three Visits + Farseek
rows.text: secure missing colors with typed dual lands. Lore and Visits find Forest cards; Farseek finds an appropriate Plains, Island, Swamp, or Mountain card and puts it in tapped. The dual-heavy manabase supplies typed targets without relying on basic lands of every color.

rows.name: Mirari's Wake
rows.text: adds one mana whenever a land is tapped for mana and pumps your creatures. Its +1/+1 also improves Agatha's reduction and enables Kutzil's combat-draw condition for creatures whose power otherwise equals their base power.

rows.name: Smothering Tithe
rows.text: stores colored mana across turns and leaves your lands available to answer threats. Opponents can pay two to deny each Treasure. Kinnan improves a Treasure's mana activation if present, but does not make extra Treasure tokens.

guide.title: Keep drawing without a reanimation engine

rows.name: Thrasios, Triton Hero
rows.text: turns spare generic mana into lands or cards with no need for Kenrith. Creature reducers make the ability efficient, but the minimum cost is still one mana. Lands put onto the battlefield this way trigger Bill and Tracker even though they were not played from hand.

rows.name: Shorikai, Genesis Engine
rows.text: one mana and a tap gives two cards, one discard, and a Pilot. It is an independent draw engine, not a requirement to discard reanimation targets. Uncrewed, it can activate immediately when it enters and avoids creature-only removal; Muse untaps it each opposing turn.

rows.name: Tireless Tracker
rows.text: converts land drops and fetchlands into Clues, then grows as you sacrifice those Clues. This supplies cards and a larger attacker without needing opponents to search or a creature in the graveyard. Zirda discounts a Clue activation to one mana; creature-only reducers do not.

rows.name: Esper Sentinel
rows.text: Kenrith's counters, Bill, and Wake can increase its power, making opponents' payment harder. It triggers on each opponent's first noncreature spell each turn, not every spell.

rows.name: Sylvan Library + Mystic Remora
rows.text: efficient independent access to cards while you assemble mana. Pay Library's life cost only when the additional cards matter; let Remora expire when its upkeep costs more than the expected benefit. Kenrith's lifegain can replenish life later, but still costs mana.

rows.name: Faerie Mastermind + Loran of the Third Path
rows.text: Mastermind rewards opposing second draws, while Loran selectively shares a draw after removing an artifact or enchantment. Use the additional cards as bargaining tools only when the recipient is unlikely to win from them. Mastermind's activated ability draws for everyone.

rows.name: Kutzil, Malamet Exemplar
rows.text: stops opponents casting spells during your turn and draws when creatures with power above their base power connect with a player. A counter, Wake's anthem, or a pump effect can qualify a creature. Multiple qualifying creatures hitting one player together produce one draw; hitting different players can produce multiple draws. Opposing activated and triggered abilities still work.

guide.title: Make counters do more than increase damage

rows.name: Bristly Bill, Spine Sower
rows.text: landfall seeds counters, and his activated ability doubles counters on every creature you control. Creature reducers remove the generic portion but never the GG. Double counters to grow a threatening board, amplify Agatha, or stock Ballista; this is finite growth paid for with mana.

rows.name: Willbreaker + Kenrith, the Returned King
rows.text: target an opposing creature with Kenrith's green ability. Willbreaker's trigger resolves first and takes the creature, then Kenrith adds the counter. You keep it only for as long as you control Willbreaker; protect that fragile link before committing to a stolen army.

rows.name: Willbreaker + Bristly Bill, Spine Sower
rows.text: aim Bill's landfall counter at an opposing creature to take it without paying a Kenrith activation. Hexproof, shroud, and relevant protection can prevent targeting. This is a temporary control relationship tied to Willbreaker, not permanent ownership.

rows.name: Zirda, the Dawnwaker + Willbreaker
rows.text: Zirda's one-mana tap ability can target an opposing creature and trigger the theft. That creature also cannot block for the rest of the turn, so use Kenrith's counter ability instead when you want the stolen creature available as a blocker.

rows.name: Glen Elendra Archmage + Kenrith, the Returned King
rows.text: sacrifice Archmage for U to counter a noncreature spell, then let persist return it with a -1/-1 counter. Kenrith's green counter cancels that counter through state-based actions, enabling another persist return later. This uses mana for every cycle and only counters noncreature spells; it is not a free universal lock.

rows.name: Shalai, Voice of Plenty
rows.text: protects you and your other creatures from targeting, while her activated ability gives the whole team counters. Shalai herself does not get hexproof from her own ability. Use her team counters to seed creatures before Bill doubles them, or to reset a persisted Archmage when it is convenient.

guide.title: Use answers appropriate to the threat

rows.name: Scavenging Ooze
rows.text: repeated graveyard exile on a cheap creature gives you interaction without reanimating anything. Exiling a creature adds a counter and life, making Ooze a relevant attacker. Its G cost is already entirely colored and cannot be reduced.

rows.name: Soul-Guide Lantern
rows.text: a one-mana safety valve against graveyard combos when Ooze would require too many activations. Sacrificing it exiles opponents' graveyards while preserving yours. Do not sacrifice it for a card if an opponent is about to use the graveyard to win.

rows.name: Swords to Plowshares + Path to Exile
rows.text: efficient exile for creatures you cannot safely steal or leave in a graveyard. The controller's compensation is usually preferable to letting a winning creature remain.

rows.name: Anguished Unmaking + Assassin's Trophy + Generous Gift
rows.text: broad permanent removal that covers artifacts, enchantments, planeswalkers, and creatures. Trophy and Gift can also answer a specific problematic land; this is targeted interaction, not a mass land-denial plan.

rows.name: Pest Infestation
rows.text: removes up to X artifacts or enchantments and gives you twice X Pests. Pay 2X+G, not X+G. You may choose zero targets and simply build a board, and with zero targets it cannot fail because a targeted permanent disappeared. Targeted casts still depend on at least one target remaining legal.

rows.name: Mystic Confluence
rows.text: choose three modes, repeating modes if useful: tax a spell by three, bounce a creature, or draw a card. It is particularly useful when holding up mana because you can refill if nobody presents a threat. The counter mode is a payment tax, not an unconditional counter.

rows.name: Arcane Denial + Dovin's Veto + Swan Song
rows.text: efficient stack interaction preserves enough mana for development. Use Veto for a crucial noncreature spell, Song when its restricted card types fit, and Denial when you need to stop a creature spell as well. They do not counter activated abilities.

rows.name: Krosan Grip
rows.text: clears an artifact or enchantment that shuts off activations or threatens a win. Split second does not suppress mana abilities or triggered abilities, but prevents ordinary spell and nonmana-ability responses while Grip is on the stack.

rows.name: Profane Procession
rows.text: retained as a useful exile-and-theft tool, rather than the entire plan. Zirda reduces each front-face activation from 3WB to 1WB; the creature-only reducers do not. After three captured cards it transforms, and the land face can deploy those particular exiled creatures under your control.

cards.name: Profane Procession // Tomb of the Dusk Rose

rows.text: Profane Procession has no tap cost on its front. With enough mana, hold priority and stack additional activations before one transforms it; already-pending activations can still exile their targets. Tokens do not count as captured cards. Commanders moved out of exile are not available to steal later, and the transformed land has a finite supply of captured creatures. Muse can untap the land on opponents' turns.

rows.name: Toxic Deluge + Austere Command
rows.text: reset a losing board when individual answers are insufficient. Deluge also kills your dorks and reducers, while Command's selected modes can hit your own artifacts or enchantments. Keep lands and independent draw where possible so the reset does not leave you unable to rebuild.

guide.title: Finish with the battlefield you have built

rows.name: Adeline, Resplendent Cathar
rows.text: whenever you attack, she supplies a tapped attacking Human for each opponent, even if Adeline herself stayed home. Kenrith, Shalai, Bill, Wake, and Finale turn that growing board into damage. Tokens entering attacking did not themselves attack for attack-trigger purposes.

rows.name: Koma, Cosmos Serpent
rows.text: a standalone threat that produces a 3/3 Serpent on EVERY upkeep. Sacrifice another Serpent to protect Koma from destruction or tap a key permanent and disable its activated abilities for that turn. Tap attackers before attackers are declared; tapping an already attacking creature does not remove it from combat.

rows.name: Koma, Cosmos Serpent + Kenrith, the Returned King
rows.text: Coil production supplies an army while Kenrith supplies haste and trample. Koma also works with Kenrith absent, making it a useful threat to cast directly instead of a dedicated reanimation target. Its indestructibility option does not stop exile or sacrifice.

rows.name: Finale of Devastation
rows.text: at X at least ten, the team gets +X/+X and haste even if the searched creature is merely a useful support piece. Kenrith can add trample. At smaller X, fetch the missing engine or answer; the primary plan is to search the library, with graveyard access available as backup.

rows.name: Walking Ballista + Bristly Bill, Spine Sower
rows.text: seed Ballista with counters, double them across available mana windows, then remove counters for direct damage. Kenrith can add a counter for as little as G with a reducer. Without Wake's anthem or another toughness boost, do not remove the final counter until you are ready for Ballista to die.

rows.name: Willbreaker + Walking Ballista
rows.text: target an opposing creature with a one-damage activation to take it before the damage resolves. Choose a creature that survives the damage. This spends a counter each time, and removing Willbreaker returns the creatures; it is not free permanent theft. Ballista returned by Kenrith normally dies immediately with zero counters unless another effect already gives it sufficient toughness.

rows.name: Boros Charm
rows.text: protect all your permanents from destruction or give a large attacker double strike. Kenrith adds trample to push that damage through blockers. The four-damage mode can finish a low-life player or remove a planeswalker, but is rarely the main use.

guide.title: Protect the engine that matters now

rows.name: Grand Abolisher + Kutzil, Malamet Exemplar
rows.text: make your own turn safer when committing to a tutor, theft sequence, or lethal attack. Abolisher also restricts opponents' activated abilities from artifacts, creatures, and enchantments. Neither protects you during opponents' turns, and neither stops all triggered abilities.

rows.name: Heroic Intervention + Veil of Summer
rows.text: inexpensive protection lets you continue developing without abandoning interaction. Intervention does not stop exile sweepers, sacrifice, or toughness reduction; Veil's hexproof concerns blue and black and does not stop an untargeted overloaded spell.

rows.name: Clever Concealment + Teferi's Protection
rows.text: phase out key permanents through threats that indestructibility cannot solve. Your tokens can convoke Concealment, including newly created tokens, but phased-out engines are unavailable until they return. Concealment cannot phase out lands; Protection also preserves your life total until your next turn.

Kenrith's black activation recovers a lost Muse, reducer, or utility creature when useful. Avoid holding expensive creatures in hand waiting for them to die or filling the graveyard just to activate it. Against graveyard hate, continue with mana, counters, theft, draw, and combat rather than treating the deck as switched off.

guide.title: Tutors are decisions, not a fixed reanimation script

rows.name: Eladamri's Call -> Seedborn Muse
rows.text: find the untapper when you have mana sources and an ability worth using each turn. If mana production itself is weak, Incubation Druid or Kinnan may be a more useful first target.

rows.name: Formidable Speaker -> Shalai, Voice of Plenty
rows.text: find protection for an engine that is otherwise exposed to targeted removal. Speaker requires discarding a card to tutor; discard a redundant card, not a mandatory reanimation target. The found creature goes to hand.

rows.name: Formidable Speaker -> Willbreaker
rows.text: find theft when opponents have creatures worth taking and you already have a targeting ability. Without that setup, prefer an independent threat such as Koma or a mana engine.

rows.name: Formidable Speaker
rows.text: once it can tap, one mana untaps another permanent. Use it on a productive mana creature, Shorikai, or a needed land. It cannot untap itself, so this is another finite resource conversion, not an infinite mana loop.

rows.name: Chord of Calling -> Glen Elendra Archmage
rows.text: put a counterspell creature onto the battlefield at instant speed, but leave U to activate it. You can cast Chord in response to the spell you need to counter. Only green creatures can convoke its green pips, and a creature used for convoke cannot also tap for mana to pay for the same spell.

rows.name: Chord of Calling -> Scavenging Ooze
rows.text: fetch graveyard interaction in response to a recursion spell, leaving G for the exile activation. If you spend every available mana on Chord, finding Ooze does not itself exile the target.

rows.name: Finale of Devastation -> Koma, Cosmos Serpent
rows.text: a mana-rich line when you need a standalone board engine. Koma costs X=7 here, making Finale nine mana; casting Koma from hand is cheaper, so this is access to the threat rather than a way to cheat its cost.

rows.name: Kinnan, Bonder Prodigy
rows.text: his discounted top-five activation can find non-Human creatures such as Muse, Incubation Druid, Shalai, Glen Elendra Archmage, or Koma. It can miss, and it cannot put Humans such as Kenrith, Willbreaker, Adeline, or Tracker into play. Check the actual creature type before relying on a hit.

Keep three usable lands, early ramp, and either an inexpensive answer or a draw engine. A strong example is Command Tower, Savannah, Underground Sea, Birds of Paradise, Nature's Lore, Esper Sentinel, and Swords to Plowshares. Mulligan hands with several five-mana engines and no way to deploy them, even if they have all five colors.

Develop green mana first, then the colors of the actual spells in hand. Deploy a mana creature or land ramp before loading the board with reducers. Kenrith need not be the first five-mana play: Muse may provide more immediate value if you already have Shorikai or Thrasios active, while a pressured board may require removal instead.

With Seedborn Muse, budget each opponent's turn separately. Preserve the colored mana for an urgent answer, then use surplus mana before the next untap on draw, counters, or tokens already available. Do not automatically spend all black mana on recovery when green counters or blue cards better advance the board.

When you have enough cards and mana, stop drawing for its own sake. Seed counters, build bodies, protect Willbreaker if using theft, and count a Finale or Ballista finish. Kenrith's red activation helps everyone, so be cautious using it before an opponent's combat or after giving an opponent a creature back.

This deck has no intentional infinite-mana or reanimation loop. It is strongest when you adapt to the table: graveyard exile against recursion, stack interaction against spell wins, theft against creature piles, and tokens plus counters against slow value decks. Repeated engine removal and restrictions on activated abilities remain real weaknesses; prioritize the answers that reopen your most useful options.
